issue_context.title: Refactoring against runtime FieldType

review_comments:
Needed. Since fields are made private, json encoder/decoder will not encode/decoded these fields anymore. That said we need a custom encoder/decoder, and jsonFieldType is for that purpose...

This is a unavoidable limitation if we want to make fields private, sadly.
Why do we need both NewFieldTypeBuilder and NewFieldTypeBuilderP ?

The motivation is to have a chain builder to replace `newFt := xxx(); newFt.SetXXX(); newFt.SetXXX();`. Of course, `newFT()` could be of type `fn () *FieldType` such that `NewFT().SetXXX().SetXXX()` can be implemented, but that may be escaped while plain `FieldType` is embedding in some structs. If `newFT()` returns a pointer, then it can not be inlined.

Another point is to wrap around `FieldType`, to make the construction consistent. There are too many ways to construct `FieldType`, by exported types or various constructors. I hope we could build `FieldType` by only one API.
Should we set `element.clone()` to `ft.elems[idx]`? I think it is unsafe to directly assign the value.

That is a logic changer. This PR so far, try to avoid logic changes as much as possible. Only setters/getters, field type builder are added to make things consistent. I think it is too early to adjust COW or any other read/write isolation mechanism.

BTW, my preference would be a read only `FieldType` by default, and explicitly copy `MutableFieldType`.
Why do we need these `Set` funcs for Builder?

@xhebox  is the file creator.  The motivation to get minor performance benefit from avoidance of escape analysis.  There were multiple places to construct fieldtype with various number of attributes. We provide the builder mode plus setter methods to avoid introducing too many constructors.

The reason of not exporting internal `FieldType` is for future, where you might want to introduce more complex construction logic into the builder, to control the behavior of construction, or even modification of `FieldType`s.

As you may think, if builder is only thin wrapper of `FieldType`, then there is no need to hide the internal `FieldType`.

However, even if there is no builder, the changes of `setter/getter` are really huge anyway. It will be thouands of lines anyway, then  why not leave some *unneeded* changes for possible future? It doesn't hurt anyway.
